name: Fix a kube-bench kubelet-config FAIL
objective: CKS › Cluster Setup + System Hardening (10% + 15%). Drill the kube-bench workflow harder than the exam: run it as a Job against node AND master, read [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN], then remediate every recurring finding — manifest & PKI file modes, the kubelet read-only port, the apiserver NodeRestriction plugin — plus a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a kube-bench kubelet-config FAIL
questions.teach:
CIS 4.1.9 wants the kubelet config file `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` at mode `0600` or stricter — it holds the kubelet's security settings. kube-bench names the file and expected mode in its `[FAIL]` line; confirm with `stat -c '%a'`.

**Gotcha:** this is a `chmod`-only fix — do NOT restart the kubelet, and don't confuse the file's mode with its `readOnlyPort` content from the previous step.
questions.prompt:
kube-bench reports a `[FAIL]` for the kubelet config file permissions on worker `$W1` — setup loosened `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` to mode `644`. Diagnose which file and mode CIS expects, then fix it. No hint beyond the kube-bench output. Do NOT restart the kubelet.

Target: `docker exec $W1 stat -c '%a' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` prints `600` (and the file still contains `readOnlyPort: 0` from the prior step).
questions.hint: Re-run kube-bench node (or just `docker exec $W1 stat -c '%a' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`) — it's `644`, CIS 4.1.9 wants `600`. `docker exec $W1 chmod 600 /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`.
questions.solution:
# kube-bench 4.1.9: /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml must be 600 or more restrictive.
docker exec $W1 stat -c '%a' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml   # 644 -> too open
docker exec $W1 chmod 600 /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
docker exec $W1 stat -c '%a' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml   # 600

verification.description: kubelet config file on $W1 is exactly mode 600 (diagnose-and-fix)
